newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan trade gap makes sense in economic terms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan trade gap makes sense in economic terms.

text.p: Brazil's $413 million trade deficit in January makes sense in economic terms when compared with average imports and exports over the past six months, said a senior Finance Ministry official.

Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary at the Finance Ministry, also said problems with registering fuel imports by state oil firm Petrobras had been resolved by January 22 and would not reoccur in coming months.

Mendonca de Barros said imports of $4.098 billion for the in the new Siscomex automatic import documentation system resulted because Petrobras had always had unique import procedures, registering its purchases after they were offloaded.
He said Petrobras took longer than expected to adapt to the new system of registering imports before offloading because of "bureaucratic problems" and inefficiencies.
"In February, the (Siscomex) system is already perfectly normalized," he said. "Petrobras has adapted now completely to the new system."
Mendonca de Barros said oil imports were the only inconsistency identified by officials in the trade figures.
He fervently denied media speculation that the government was trying to "hide" a large deficit and insisted that Siscomex itself did not result in any distortions.

"There was no drop in deliveries because of Siscomex," he said, adding he could not say whether some importers might have reprogrammed their imports for February because of teething problems with the system in early January.

Mendonca de Barros said the government had settled on Petrobras oil imports of $473 million for the month as the real figure. Some remaining $120 million of gasoline which has not been officially processed will be added to February's imports.
